subject: Evoke invoice: unexpected metering surge on May statement
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <billing@evoke.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: May invoice — sharp metering spike (need logs)

Hi Grace,

We received Invoice EVK-2026-05 this morning and it looks 4-5x higher than our normal monthly consumption. Quick summary: billed tokens ~3.2M vs our usual ~700k. The charge lines point to the text-generation endpoint and an increased count on the "aux-model" routing.

Can you provide: a raw usage export (per-request with request_id / model / route / tenant_tag), any traces showing retries/backfills, and the original invoice PDF. We need this for our internal finance review — if this is an internal integration bug on our side we will admit it, but the numbers are unexpected.

Attached: invoice-EVK-2026-05.pdf (we attached for reference).

Thanks,
Ethan Cole
Finance Manager, Evoke Systems
billing@evoke.com

--

Date: 2026-05-20T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: May invoice — sharp metering spike (need logs)

Hi Ethan — thanks for flagging this. I'm looping in Ben (billing ops) and Jordan (your AM) so we can triage quickly.

Immediate plan:
- Ben: we'll pull a per-request export for May 18-21 (CSV with request_id, model, endpoint, token_in, token_out, tenant_tag, user_agent).
- We'll also export server-side traces for any high-volume request IDs and check if any routing fallbacks/aux models caused double accounting.
- I'll aim to send a first-pass findings and the export by EOD 5/21.

Can you confirm whether Evoke ran any scheduled backfills or large batch re-ingests around May 18-21, and whether any staging keys might have been used? That would help narrow tenant_tag attribution.

Appreciate the patience — we'll treat this as high priority.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: initial forensic notes for EVK spike

Grace / Jordan — I pulled the per-request export and a few quick observations:

1) Volume breakdown (May 18-21) — total billed tokens ~3.15M.
   - ~1.9M tokens originate from requests with a common user_agent "evoke-backfill/1.2" and request_ids that share the prefix "evk-bf-".
   - ~850k tokens from normal interactive sessions (unique session ids).
   - ~400k tokens flagged as "aux-model-reroute" where our routing system fell back to a compatibility model.

2) Tenant attribution — ~1.85M of the backfill-prefixed requests have tenant_tag unset (NULL) in the metadata. Those requests still carried Evoke's customer_id in the header, but because tenant_tag was missing they were attributed to the default production owner for billing. It appears a missing client-side header in an older SDK version caused tenant_tag to be dropped during the batch job.

3) Duplicate/Retry patterns — about 7% of the backfill request_ids show retry suffixes ("-r1", "-r2") within short windows; some retries seem to have been replayed by an ingestion orchestrator.

4) Recommended interim remediation
   - Offer a provisional credit for the portion clearly attributable to a backfill + tenant_tag bug (we estimate 60% of the spike), pending Evoke confirming the job.
   - Provide the full request-trace bundle and a CSV export for their auditors.

I've packaged the evidence files and a trimmed trace list in the shared drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleEvidence (files: EVK_usage_export_20260520.csv, request-traces-evoke-20260520.log, supporting-telemetry-snippets.txt).

If you want a draft credit calculation, I can run numbers now.

Ben
Billing Ops — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

--
Attachment: EVK_usage_export_20260520.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)
Attachment: request-traces-evoke-20260520.log (LOG, 3.6MB)
Attachment: supporting-telemetry-snippets.txt (TXT, 24KB)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <billing@evoke.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-22T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: May invoice — sharp metering spike (need logs)

Hi Ethan — following up with root-cause and a proposal. Apologies for the disruption.

Summary: Ben's analysis indicates ~1.9M billed tokens were generated by an Evoke backfill job that omitted tenant_tag in ~98% of requests. Those requests were still authenticated with Evoke's customer_id but were billed to production because tenant_tag metadata was empty. There were also some retries (~7% of that set) that increased token counts further.

Proposal:
- Redwood will issue a one-time credit of $8,740 to offset the portion of May charges attributable to the tenant_tag/backfill bug. Credit will appear on the June invoice (reference: credit EVK-CR-2026-05).
- We will provide the full export and traces (attached) for Evoke's audit.
- Ben and our engineering PM will coordinate a short call with your SREs to confirm SDK header behavior and recommend a small safeguard we can add server-side to prevent untagged backfills from being billed to prod in the future.

Next steps for you: please confirm receipt of the attachments and confirm whether Evoke ran any backfill jobs on May 18-21 so we can finalize the credit math. If you accept the credit proposal we'll apply it to June's statement and close the ticket.

Thanks again for raising this quickly — Jordan will follow up on scheduling the SRE call.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
